title: Inverse image of the torsor extension
statement: Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. For a $G$-torsor $T$, let $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ be the canonical extension used in [lem-sc-torsor-h1], whose fibre over $1$ is $T$. Then inverse image along $u$ carries this short exact sequence to $0\to u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}E_T\to\mathbf Z_Y\to0$, and the resulting extension is canonically the extension $E_{u^{-1}T}$ attached to the inverse-image torsor: the inverse image $u^{-1}T$ of the sheaf of sets $T$, with the inverse image of the action map $G\times T\to T$ (via $u^{-1}(G\times T)=u^{-1}G\times u^{-1}T$), is a $u^{-1}G$-torsor, and there is a unique isomorphism of extensions $u^{-1}E_T\cong E_{u^{-1}T}$ which is the identity on $u^{-1}G$, is the identification $u^{-1}\mathbf Z_X\cong\mathbf Z_Y$ on the quotients, and sends $u^{-1}[t]$ to $[u^{-1}t]$ for local sections $t$ of $T$; it restricts on fibres over $1$ to the identity of $u^{-1}T$, compatibly with the $u^{-1}G$-actions.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (label lemma-torsors-h1), functoriality of the extension E_T: u^{-1}E_T = E_{u^{-1}T}

proof.text: Write $\mathbf Z[S]$ for the free abelian sheaf on a sheaf of sets $S$ (sheafified formal sums, as in [lem-sc-torsor-h1]); by the universal properties of free abelian groups and of sheafification, $\mathrm{Hom}_{\Ab}(\mathbf Z[S],A)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sets}}(S,A)$ naturally, and $\mathbf Z_X=\mathbf Z[*]$ for the final sheaf $*$. The construction of [lem-sc-torsor-h1] reads: $E_T=\mathrm{coker}(\rho_T)$ with $\rho_T:\mathbf Z[G\times T]\to G\oplus\mathbf Z[T]$, $[(g,t)]\mapsto g+[t]-[g\cdot t]$, $\iota_T:G\to E_T$ the inclusion of the summand and $\sigma_T:E_T\to\mathbf Z_X$, $[t]\mapsto1$, $G\mapsto0$, giving the short exact sequence $0\to G\to E_T\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] the abelian inverse image $u^{-1}$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is exact and additive, so it preserves direct sums and cokernels: $u^{-1}E_T=\mathrm{coker}(u^{-1}\rho_T)$ and $0\to u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}E_T\to u^{-1}\mathbf Z_X\to0$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures](1)-(3) the underlying sheaf of sets of the abelian $u^{-1}$ is the set inverse image, which commutes with finite limits (so $u^{-1}*=*$, $u^{-1}(G\times T)=u^{-1}G\times u^{-1}T$), and the abelian and set adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ agree on underlying sets. Hence for any sheaf of sets $S$ on $X_{\Et}$ and $A\in\Ab(Y_{\Et})$, naturally in $A$: $\mathrm{Hom}(u^{-1}\mathbf Z[S],A)=\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf Z[S],u_*A)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sets}}(S,u_*A)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sets}}(u^{-1}S,A)=\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf Z[u^{-1}S],A)$; by Yoneda there is a unique isomorphism $\theta_S:u^{-1}\mathbf Z[S]\to\mathbf Z[u^{-1}S]$ with $\theta_S(u^{-1}[s])=[u^{-1}s]$, natural in $S$. For $S=*$ this gives $u^{-1}\mathbf Z_X\cong\mathbf Z_Y$ with $1\mapsto1$, which on underlying sets is the isomorphism $\gamma_u$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] (the unique morphism with $u^*1\mapsto1$ there, for $E=\mathbf Z$, by additivity on $u^*\eta(e)$). This gives the displayed sequence $0\to u^{-1}G\to u^{-1}E_T\to\mathbf Z_Y\to0$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (label lemma-torsors-h1), inverse image of the free abelian sheaf and of the extension sequence

proof.text: Fibres over $1$. For any short exact sequence $0\to H\to E\xrightarrow{\sigma}\mathbf Z\to0$ of abelian sheaves, the subsheaf $F=\sigma^{-1}(1)$ (the fibre product $E\times_{\mathbf Z}*$ along $1$), with $H$ acting by translation, is an $H$-torsor in the sense of [def-sc-gm-torsor]: the action is free, it is transitive since the difference of two local sections of $F$ lies in $\ker\sigma=H$, and $F$ has sections locally since $\sigma$ is surjective as a map of sheaves, and a local section $f$ gives $H|\cong F|$, $h\mapsto h+f$. For $E_T$, the map $T\to\sigma_T^{-1}(1)$, $t\mapsto[t]$, is $G$-equivariant since $[g\cdot t]=[t]+g$ in $E_T$, and an equivariant map of $G$-torsors is an isomorphism (locally both are $G$ and the map is translation by a section); so the fibre of $E_T$ over $1$ is $T$. The set inverse image commutes with this fibre product and with the action map [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures](1),(3), and $u^{-1}(1)=1$ by Step 1; hence $u^{-1}T$, with the inverse-image action, is identified $u^{-1}G$-equivariantly with the fibre over $1$ of $u^{-1}E_T\to\mathbf Z_Y$, and by the general fact just proved it is a $u^{-1}G$-torsor. Thus $E_{u^{-1}T}$ is defined.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03AJ (label lemma-torsors-h1), fibre over 1 and torsor structure

proof.text: Identification. Under $\theta_{G\times T}$ and $\theta_T$ of Step 1 and $u^{-1}(G\times T)=u^{-1}G\times u^{-1}T$, the map $u^{-1}\rho_T$ becomes $\rho_{u^{-1}T}$: both are additive maps out of a free abelian sheaf, so by the universal property they are determined by their values on the generators $[(g,t)]$ ($g,t$ local sections of $u^{-1}G,u^{-1}T$), and both send $[(g,t)]$ to $g+[t]-[g\cdot t]$, the action on $u^{-1}T$ being the inverse image of the action of $G$ on $T$ (Step 2). Hence $\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}G}\oplus\theta_T$ induces an isomorphism $u^{-1}E_T=\mathrm{coker}(u^{-1}\rho_T)\cong\mathrm{coker}(\rho_{u^{-1}T})=E_{u^{-1}T}$; it commutes with the inclusions of $u^{-1}G$ and, on generators, with $u^{-1}\sigma_T$ and $\sigma_{u^{-1}T}$ (both $[t]\mapsto1$, $u^{-1}G\mapsto0$), so it is an isomorphism of extensions, unique with these properties because $u^{-1}G$ and the $[u^{-1}t]$ generate. On fibres over $1$ it sends $[u^{-1}t]$ to $[u^{-1}t]$, so under the identifications of Step 2 it is the identity of $u^{-1}T$, compatible with the $u^{-1}G$-actions. So the pulled-back extension is canonically $E_{u^{-1}T}$ with fibre $u^{-1}T$ over $1$.
